blurb: Got a toddler who needs to run around and touch some dirt? Lewisville's Toddler Nature Time on Wednesday morning is made for exactly that. It's 90 minutes of outdoor exploration designed for the little ones — structured enough to hold their attention, loose enough that they're actually just playing outside. Free, local, and the kind of thing where you show up once and start putting it on the calendar every time it comes back around. If you've got a kid in that 2-to-5 range who's been cooped up, this is a Wednesday win.
scoring_notes: Family-heavy audience with a median age of 36 means a real concentration of parents with toddlers. Strong audience match. Uniqueness is lower because it likely recurs, but it's being flagged here as a useful calendar entry for the family segment. Scored conservatively on uniqueness.

blurb: Sunday afternoon, Lewisville is hosting a reception for "She Found Her Way," a new exhibition featuring works by artist Crys Nelson. Receptions like this are genuinely underrated — you get to walk through the work while the artist is actually in the room, which changes how you see everything. It runs from 3 to 5 PM, it's free, and it's the kind of low-key, interesting afternoon that doesn't require a reservation or a babysitter. If you've been looking for something a little different to do with the weekend before it's gone, this is a solid call.
scoring_notes: The reception (vs. the exhibition itself) is a one-time event with a can't-miss element — the artist is likely present. Free, low-commitment, and suits the educated, mixed-age audience. Less family-coded but fits the adult portion of the readership well. Free entry with an optional upgrade (reserved tables) fits all income levels and the mixed family/adult audience. R&B and pop programming has broad appeal across the 38-year-old median age group.

blurb: Juanes is one of the biggest Latin rock artists alive, with more than two decades of records, a shelf full of Grammy Awards, and a live show that earns its reputation. The fit depends on audience familiarity with Latin rock, which is moderate for this demographic profile. Wednesday night is a slight friction point for families but less so for young professionals and empty nesters who make up a solid portion of this audience.

blurb: The Phillies are coming to Truist Park on Friday, September 11th, and this is a matchup worth showing up for. scoring_notes: The Phillies matchup scores slightly higher on uniqueness than the Rays series because Philadelphia is a marquee NL opponent with a competitive recent history, making the game feel more like an event. Friday night first pitch at 7:15 is ideal for the working professional segment of this audience. Strong across family and adult-skewing segments alike.

venue: Sandy Springs Performing Arts Center, Sandy Springs
blurb: Les Misérables is coming to the Sandy Springs Performing Arts Center, and if you've never seen it live, this is the one to go to. Not a movie, not a soundtrack on a road trip. The real thing, performed on a stage ten minutes from home. It's been running somewhere in the world for over 40 years because it is genuinely that good. The music alone, I Dreamed a Dream, One Day More, On My Own, hits different when there are real voices filling a room. Grab tickets, grab dinner beforehand, and make a proper night of it.
scoring_notes: Sandy Springs Performing Arts Center is directly inside the coverage area, which is a major relevance boost. The educated, higher-income Perimeter audience skews toward arts and culture events. Les Mis is one of the most celebrated musicals in history, giving it strong name recognition across age groups. The mix of young professionals, adults, and empty nesters all have reason to attend.

event_name: Chance the Rapper at Coca-Cola Roxy
blurb: Chance the Rapper is one of those artists people have been meaning to see live for years, and September 3rd at Coca-Cola Roxy is a real shot to finally do it. He built his name releasing music for free, winning three Grammys before he ever sold an album, and putting on shows that feel more like a celebration than a concert. The Roxy is a great mid-size venue, which means you're close enough to actually feel it. This isn't a stadium show where you're watching a screen. Tickets are moving, so if you've been thinking about it, stop thinking.
scoring_notes: Median age of 38 puts this audience squarely in the Chance the Rapper fanbase, which peaked in cultural relevance in the 2010s when this cohort was in their mid-to-late 20s. High income means ticket price is no barrier. Coca-Cola Roxy is close enough to the Perimeter to be a realistic night out. Uniqueness is solid as a single-night concert event.

event_name: Harry Potter and the Sorcerer's Stone at Springs Cinema & Taphouse
blurb: This one is literally in your backyard, and it's the kind of night that's hard to say no to. Springs Cinema is screening Harry Potter and the Sorcerer's Stone on Sunday, and if you haven't done a movie night there yet, this is the one to finally make it happen. scoring_notes: Springs Cinema is directly in the Perimeter coverage area, which instantly boosts relevance. The taphouse format skews adult while the Harry Potter IP also works for families with older kids, covering both segments of this mixed audience. $105K household income is a non-issue for this price point. Special screening of a classic film at a local dine-in venue beats a standard movie night and gives it enough uniqueness to feature.

blurb: If you've heard "Stargazing" on the radio or seen it blow up on social media in the last year, you already know Myles Smith. If you haven't, here's the short version: he's a British singer-songwriter with a voice that sounds like it was built for late nights and big rooms, and he's having a breakout moment right now. However, his crossover pop-soul sound has broader appeal than a niche artist would. Included because the Roxy venue is familiar and local-adjacent, and the 'catch them early' framing resonates with the educated, culturally curious East Cobb reader.

event_name: Chance The Rapper at Coca-Cola Roxy
blurb: Chance The Rapper at the Roxy is a legitimate get. He's one of the more interesting figures in modern hip-hop, an artist who built a massive following without ever signing to a major label, released a Grammy-winning mixtape for free, and has been selective enough about touring that when he does show up, it means something. The Roxy is an intimate room by concert standards, which means you're close. This is not a stadium show where he's a dot in the distance. Thursday night, Battery Ave. Check road closure advisories before you go.
scoring_notes: Chance The Rapper has a broad enough appeal to pull in the 35-50 crowd, but this skews younger, which actually works for East Cobb given the mix of teens and college-age kids in the audience. The Roxy's intimate size is a genuine selling point. Uniqueness is high because his touring schedule is sporadic. Slightly lower demographic fit for the pure empty nester segment, but strong for families with older kids.

blurb: Free, at The Battery, the weekend before Labor Day. That's the short version. The longer version is that the Braves Block Party takes over the streets of The Battery before select home games with live entertainment, a DJ, a live chalk artist, street performers, and enough activities to keep kids and adults both occupied for hours. Kids get batting cages, base running challenges, and chalk art. Adults get tailgate games, food, drinks, and a legitimately good vibe before the game. You don't need a game ticket to enjoy the block party itself, which makes this one of the better low-commitment options if you want to be in the energy without committing to nine innings. East Cobb to The Battery is 15 minutes on a good day. Worth the trip.
scoring_notes: Strong family fit and free entry makes this very accessible. The Battery is essentially East Cobb's entertainment hub, so proximity is a selling point. Lower uniqueness score because block parties are a recurring Braves pre-game format, not a one-off event. However, the specific date (August 29) and the free, all-ages nature bump its practical appeal for this audience.

venue: Earl and Rachel Smith Strand Theatre, Marietta
blurb: Three cousins, a trailer, and Times Square. That's the setup. The 3 Redneck Tenors are back at the Strand for a show that runs through Broadway's greatest hits, Phantom of the Opera, Les Misérables, Oklahoma, Annie, South Pacific, and then wraps the whole thing in their signature Southern fried delivery that somehow makes it funnier and more fun than it has any right to be. Doors open at 2:00 PM for regular admission, seating starts at 2:30, and the show runs 3:00 to 5:00 with an intermission in the middle. Sunday afternoon, right in Marietta Square. If you've been before, you already know. If you haven't, this is an easy first date with the Strand.
scoring_notes: Good fit for established families and empty nesters looking for something lighthearted and local on a Sunday afternoon. The Strand is a beloved East Cobb-adjacent institution. Broadway content plus Southern comedy hits well for this age and income bracket. Lower uniqueness score because the 3 Redneck Tenors do tour regionally, but this is a specific dated event at a venue the audience already loves.

event_name: When Rivers Meet: The Black and Jewish Origins of America's Sound
blurb: Karla Harris and Joe Alterman are two of the most compelling performers working in this region right now, and this concert is not something you stumble across every weekend. The premise alone is worth showing up for: tracing the musical and cultural collisions between Black and Jewish communities, from Harlem to the Delta to Tin Pan Alley to the Brill Building. It's the origin story behind half the American music you love, told live by a vocalist and a pianist who actually know how to tell it. This is the kind of evening where you walk in curious and walk out wanting to talk about it over dinner. Roswell Cultural Arts Center is an easy drive from East Cobb. Check the link for showtime and ticket details.
scoring_notes: Strong fit for the educated, culturally engaged East Cobb audience. The subject matter rewards curiosity and historical interest, both hallmarks of this demographic. Roswell is local enough to feel accessible. Uniqueness is high because this is a specific, themed concert with named performers, not a generic show. Adult and empty nester skew, which fits the audience well.

blurb: If you've never seen Parade, this is the production to fix that. It's a Tony Award-winning musical built around one of the most haunting chapters in Georgia history: the 1913 trial of Leo Frank, a Jewish factory manager accused of murder in the middle of a state consumed by fear and political pressure. The book is by Alfred Uhry, the same guy who wrote Driving Miss Daisy, and the score is Jason Robert Brown, who doesn't miss. What makes this one different from a standard musical is that it doesn't let you off easy. It's equal parts love story and gut punch, and it ends the kind of way that sits with you on the drive home. The Strand is right there in Marietta Square, so make a night of it. Dinner first, then the show. Group of 10 or more? Call the box office at 770-293-0080 for a group discount.
scoring_notes: East Cobb's educated, 42-median-age audience is exactly who goes to serious regional theater. The Georgia-specific historical subject matter adds local resonance. Alfred Uhry's name carries real weight in Atlanta-area arts circles. Strong empty nester and date-night fit. The group discount mention is genuinely useful for this community.

blurb: This is not your average game day. Bats & Bites is a behind-the-scenes experience at Truist Park that gives you early access to the ballpark, a guided tour that ends at the Outfield Market, face time with a former Braves player, and samples of new featured food plus a signature beer or cocktail. Then you head out to the outfield to watch batting practice up close. Like, actually-on-the-field-level close. If you've been going to Braves games for years and think you've seen it all, this is the version of Truist Park most fans never get to see. Grab a spot before they fill up.
scoring_notes: Truist Park is East Cobb's backyard. This is a premium, access-driven experience that plays perfectly to a $118K household income audience. The former player meet-and-greet and behind-the-scenes tour make it genuinely unique, not just another game. Strong fit for established families and empty nesters alike. Adults lead this experience, but it's not exclusively adult-only.

event_name: When Rivers Meet: The Black and Jewish Origins of America's Sound
blurb:
You've hummed along to jazz standards, shouted the words to Broadway hits, and felt something in your chest when the blues comes on. But do you actually know the story behind where that music came from? Probably not the full one.

When Rivers Meet is a live performance that traces the unlikely creative partnership between Black and Jewish artists who built the soundtrack of America together, from the Mississippi Delta to Tin Pan Alley to the Brill Building. Atlanta jazz vocalist Karla Harris and pianist Joe Alterman bring it to life through live music, storytelling, and the kind of historical depth that makes familiar songs feel brand new. This is not a lecture with a piano in the corner. It's a real performance that happens to teach you something.

This one is at the Roswell Cultural Arts Center on Sunday afternoon. It fits beautifully between a late morning and a Sunday dinner out. Grab tickets before the seats fill up.
scoring_notes: Highly educated, higher-income East Cobb audience that skews toward established adults and empty nesters. A culturally rich live performance blending music history, jazz, and storytelling is almost a perfect fit. Roswell location is close and familiar. One-night event, not a recurring series.
